editorial.headline: Running a Games Arena: a Clear National and Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: For arena operators, this classification is open across all business scales, fully foreign-open nationally, and not moratorium-blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Managing a games arena is, at its core, a venue-and-facilities activity. The scope covers the provision of places and facilities for games of skill and/or gaming machines operated with coins or cards as the principal activity. Food and drink service may be added, but it is supplemental rather than the business’s defining purpose. The classification therefore centres on the operator of the arena itself: the setting in which those games and machines are made available, rather than a description of a particular game, product, or hospitality format.

That operator may register at the micro, small, medium, or large scale; all four are expressly open. The breadth matters because it accommodates operations at a range of commercial sizes without changing the record’s stated focus: the physical venue and facilities where the activity takes place. A food-and-drink offering can sit alongside the arena, but the record places it as an addition to the principal activity. The classification thus gives a clean frame for an arena-led business, whether its operating footprint is modest or large.

On foreign ownership, the national position is equally clear. The PMA status is open, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain terms, the national classification allows full foreign ownership. Bali does not convert that national openness into a moratorium block. Its status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that, at the Large scale, OSS risk is Medium-High/High. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium applies to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities; this one is expressly recorded as not blocked by that moratorium.

The result is a notably direct reading for a foreign investor considering this activity in Bali. The activity is nationally open to PMA at the 100% ceiling, and Bali’s record does not prohibit PMA registration under its risk-based moratorium. That is not an invitation to recast the business as something else: the centre remains the provision and management of the arena and its facilities, with coin- or card-operated machines and games of skill at its core. Any food and drink service stays an optional accompaniment.
